goals.name: Pricing Test Goal Harness
goals.description: Pricing Test Goal Harness [gtm-pricing-experiment] — compiled from capabilities/harnesses/hD-04-pricing-test.yaml
goals.gate: Hypothesis, baseline, guardrails, sizing, variants, rollback all present and hashed in proofpacket.json

gates.name: 0.1 Test objective declared: which pricing lever (amount, packag
gates.description: Test objective declared: which pricing lever (amount, packaging, fence, billing period) and which decision it informs
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/objective.md with lever and decision fields non-empty

gates.name: 0.2 pricing-governance and elasticity doctrine loaded
gates.command: grep -q 'guardrail' ~/.claude/skills/pricing-governance/SKILL.md && echo LOADED in session log

gates.name: 0.3 RIG coordinate stated (L1-L4; D1-D3; A1-A2)
gates.command: coordinate block in ~/.hermes/jake/pricing/session-<ts>.log parseable by jq

gates.name: 0.4 Harness tuple H_pricing declared with all 8 components
gates.description: Harness tuple H_pricing declared with all 8 components

gates.name: 1.1 Falsifiable hypothesis written: expected direction, minimum
gates.description: Falsifiable hypothesis written: expected direction, minimum detectable effect, and what result kills the variant
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/hypothesis.md contains direction, mde (numeric), and kill_criteria (>= 2 measurable conditions)

gates.name: 1.2 Baseline metrics captured from source systems before any var
gates.description: Baseline metrics captured from source systems before any variant exists: conversion rate, ARPA, refund rate, sales cycle for the affected segment
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/baseline.json with metric values, source query ids, and captured_at; jq 'keys | length >= 3' true

gates.name: 1.3 Guardrail metrics declared with tripwires: churn, support ti
gates.description: Guardrail metrics declared with tripwires: churn, support tickets, downgrade rate, brand-sentiment proxy
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/guardrails.yaml — each guardrail has metric, threshold, and alert_channel

gates.name: 1.4 Sample size / duration math shown: exposure count and test l
gates.description: Sample size / duration math shown: exposure count and test length derived from baseline rate and MDE
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/sizing.md contains the formula inputs and computed n and days; numbers trace to baseline.json values

gates.name: 2.1 Variant configuration expressed as hashed config: price poin
gates.description: Variant configuration expressed as hashed config: price points, packaging contents, eligible segment query, traffic split
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/variants.yaml validates via scripts/validate_variants.py exit 0; sha256 recorded in proofpacket

gates.name: 2.2 Rollback plan written: exact steps to restore control pricin
gates.description: Rollback plan written: exact steps to restore control pricing, including cache/feature-flag reverts
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/rollback.md with executable steps referencing variant config hash

gates.name: 2.3 Gate-D approval before any customer-visible price change: ty
gates.description: Gate-D approval before any customer-visible price change: typed APPROVE <run_id> recorded
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/gate_d.log contains APPROVE line; absent it, variants.yaml stays arm: false and session ends design-only

gates.name: 2.4 Segment isolation verified: test eligibility query excludes
gates.description: Segment isolation verified: test eligibility query excludes existing-contract accounts unless explicitly intended
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/eligibility_report.json shows excluded_count and the exclusion rule strings

gates.name: 3.1 Measurement plan executed against the same metric definition
gates.description: Measurement plan executed against the same metric definitions as baseline (no mid-test metric redefinition)
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/measurement.json uses identical source query ids as baseline.json; diff of definitions is empty

gates.name: 3.2 Guardrail review: every tripwire checked at analysis time; a
gates.description: Guardrail review: every tripwire checked at analysis time; any tripped guardrail forces variant stop recommendation regardless of primary result
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/guardrail_review.json with per-guardrail status; if any 'tripped', decision.md must contain stop recommendation

gates.name: 3.3 Decision recorded: scale | kill | iterate, with reasoning ti
gates.description: Decision recorded: scale | kill | iterate, with reasoning tied to hypothesis and guardrails
gates.command: artifacts/pricing/<run>/decision.md with decision enum and >= 3 reasoning bullets citing measurement numbers

gates.name: 3.4 Learning logged to pricing council: result feeds the pricing
gates.description: Learning logged to pricing council: result feeds the pricing decision log for future tests
gates.command: append to ~/.hermes/jake/pricing/council_log.md with run_id, hypothesis hash, decision, and one lesson

preconditions.startup_phrase: Pricing test session. Price is a promise; tests are contracts. Baseline before variant, guardrails before launch, decision log before memory fades.
preconditions.harness_tuple: H_pricing(hypothesis, baseline, guardrails, variants, sizing, approval, measurement, decision)
preconditions.bms_bias: A1 for metrics capture and gating; A2 for analysis; A3 only for variant ideation; A4 never — price changes are Gate-D

self_improvement.update_trigger: same gate fails 3+ times; a tripped guardrail in production triggers immediate harness review of threshold defaults

success_conditions: Hypothesis, baseline, guardrails, sizing, variants, rollback all present and hashed in proofpacket.json
Any customer-visible change shows Gate-D approval for this run_id
Decision recorded with guardrail review attached; design-only is a valid complete outcome when approval is absent
Identity closure: coordinate, verdict (designed | approved-live | analyzed), next safe action in session log
failure_states: stop gate(s) 2.3: session halts; human Gate-D approval required before any continuation or outward action
halt gate(s) 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3: no progress without gate evidence
degrade gate(s) 3.4: continue with deficit logged in the Definition of Done waiver
quality_criteria: Test objective declared: which pricing lever (amount, packaging, fence, billing period) and which decision it informs
Harness tuple H_pricing declared with all 8 components
Falsifiable hypothesis written: expected direction, minimum detectable effect, and what result kills the variant
Baseline metrics captured from source systems before any variant exists: conversion rate, ARPA, refund rate, sales cycle for the affected segment
Guardrail metrics declared with tripwires: churn, support tickets, downgrade rate, brand-sentiment proxy
Sample size / duration math shown: exposure count and test length derived from baseline rate and MDE
Variant configuration expressed as hashed config: price points, packaging contents, eligible segment query, traffic split
Rollback plan written: exact steps to restore control pricing, including cache/feature-flag reverts
Gate-D approval before any customer-visible price change: typed APPROVE <run_id> recorded
Segment isolation verified: test eligibility query excludes existing-contract accounts unless explicitly intended
Measurement plan executed against the same metric definitions as baseline (no mid-test metric redefinition)
Guardrail review: every tripwire checked at analysis time; any tripped guardrail forces variant stop recommendation regardless of primary result
Decision recorded: scale | kill | iterate, with reasoning tied to hypothesis and guardrails
Learning logged to pricing council: result feeds the pricing decision log for future tests

final_rule: No variant ships without baseline, guardrails, sizing math, and a rollback plan.
No customer-visible price change without typed Gate-D approval for this exact run.
A tripped guardrail overrides a winning primary metric. Always.
Every pricing test session leaves the system stronger than it found it.
